block-guide:
CORE/TEMPLATE-PART (Template Part) Draws a part of a block theme (header, footer, sidebar) by its slug: the theme's parts/<slug>.html file, or the copy a person saved in the Site Editor. These tools cannot read or edit theme parts: what the part shows (its menu, its logo, its words) is changed only in the Site Editor.
IN A FABREMENT TEMPLATE: USE A GLOBAL BLOCK INSTEAD A Fabrement template replaces the whole page; the theme's header and footer are not drawn. Give the frame its own header and footer as global blocks: save-synced-pattern with kind "header" / "footer", placed as <!-- wp:block {"ref":20} /-->. Those you can read and change. A template-part in the frame is accepted and, on a block theme, draws the theme's part as it is, which these tools then cannot change. Use it only when the user wants the theme's own header.
MARKUP (comment only; no HTML) <!-- wp:template-part {"slug":"header","tagName":"header"} /--> <!-- wp:template-part {"slug":"footer","tagName":"footer"} /--> slug: a part of the ACTIVE theme (get-block-source lists them under themeSettings.variations; Twenty Twenty-Five: header, header-large-title, vertical-header, footer, footer-columns, footer-newsletter, sidebar). theme: leave it out (= the active theme). A theme slug other than the active theme's finds nothing.
PITFALLS - A wrong slug or theme draws nothing for visitors; with WP_DEBUG display on it prints "Template part has been deleted or is unavailable: <slug>". - A classic theme usually has no parts: the block then draws nothing. - Changing the active theme changes or empties every placed part. - In a page's content it repeats the theme's header in the middle of the page.
CHECK Open the page as a visitor: the part appears once, where it was placed.
